{{short description|Swedish physicist}}
[[File:Professor Lars Hultman in 2024 (cropped).jpg|250px|right|thumb|Lars Hultman at the [[Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology]] in 2024]]'''Lars Hultman''' (born 1960) is a [[professor]] of [[materials science]] and head of the Division of Thin Film Physics at [[Linköping University]].<ref name="cei">[http://www.cei.se/instructors/hultman_lars.htm CEI bio page of Prof. Hultman] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100812100143/http://www.cei.se/instructors/hultman_lars.htm |date=2010-08-12 }}</ref>
Since June 2013 Hultman is the CEO of The [[Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research]] (SSF). He received his [[Ph.D.]] degree in [[Materials Science]] from [[Linköping University]] in 1988. He also did [[postdoctoral]] work at [[Northwestern University]] in 1989-1990 and was a [[visiting professor]] at [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] in 2004-2006. In 1994 he became the editor for the journal ''Vacuum''.<ref name="cei"/>

His research interests are in the [[materials science]] and [[nanotechnology]] of [[thin films]] by vapor phase deposition, in particular ion-surface interactions, microstructure evolution, and properties of advanced [[functional materials]].<ref name="cei"/>

== Awards ==
* Akzo Nobel Sweden Science Award, 2013
* [[European Research Council]], Advanced Grant.<ref name="cei"/>
* Member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]], 2009.<ref name="cei"/>
* Member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences]], 2008.<ref name="cei"/>
* Fellow of the ''Forschungszentrum Dresden-Rossendorf'', 2007.<ref name="cei"/>
* Fellow of the [[American Vacuum Society]], 2006.<ref name="cei"/>
* Jacob Wallenberg Foundation Award for Materials Science, 2000.<ref name="cei"/>
